themes_detail.label: Food Safety Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints spiked to 7 THIS WEEK versus a baseline average of 1.9 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 273% increase (z-score: 6.57)—suggesting either a new contamination or inspection pattern affecting Hillcrest/Fresh Meadows dining venues.
evidence: 7 food establishment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (273% spike, z-score 6.57)
Spike emerged suddenly this week with no prior escalation signal over the past 3 weeks
High statistical significance indicates systemic rather than random pattern
reporting_angles: Contact DOH to identify which restaurants or food service facilities are generating complaints and their violation types
Interview health inspectors about whether they've increased enforcement activity or identified a specific contamination source

themes_detail.label: Asbestos Detection Spike
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints surged 967% compared to the 8-week baseline (4 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average)—the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset (z-score: 7.49)—indicating potential building hazard discoveries across multiple properties.
evidence: 4 asbestos complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (967% spike, highest z-score: 7.49)
Spike is aged (3 weeks old) but represents most severe statistical deviation in entire dataset
Community Board has requested additional building inspectors, suggesting pre-existing inspection capacity constraints
reporting_angles: Identify the 4 buildings where asbestos was reported; investigate their age, ownership, and occupancy status
Interview DOB and EPA about whether this represents targeted enforcement or accidental discovery; assess if more buildings may be affected
Connect to Community Board's repeated budget request for more building inspectors—does this spike justify the ask?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints jumped 198% three weeks ago (16 complaints vs. 5.4 weekly average), with z-score of 3.1—suggesting environmental sanitation pressure at specific sites, though the spike is now aging.
evidence: 16 illegal dumping complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 5.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (198% spike, z-score 3.1)
Spike appeared 3 weeks ago; unclear whether trend has sustained or resolved since
Community Board has requested catch basin cleaning—may indicate broader sanitation infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: Determine whether illegal dumping complaints have continued at elevated levels this week or subsided
Map complaint locations to identify hotspots and interview DSNY about enforcement response

themes_detail.label: Maintenance & Facility Issues Double
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints doubled 3 weeks ago (8 complaints vs. 4.0 weekly average, z-score: 4.0)—raising questions about park and public facility upkeep as the district's Community Board repeatedly requests park reconstruction funding.
evidence: 8 maintenance/facility complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 4.0 weekly average (100% spike, z-score 4.0)
Community Board has year-after-year budget requests for park reconstruction and facility upgrades, suggesting chronic underfunding
Five active ULURP applications signal development pressure; unclear if complaints relate to construction or deferred maintenance
reporting_angles: Identify which parks or facilities generated the spike in complaints; assess current condition and maintenance backlog
Interview Parks Department about facility inspection schedules and funding constraints relative to Community Board requests

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Decline (Possible Data Anomaly)
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints dropped 72% THIS WEEK (10 complaints vs. 36.2 weekly average, z-score: -3.72)—a statistically significant decline that could indicate reporting lag, system error, or genuine temporary reduction; warrants verification.
evidence: 10 noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 36.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (72% decline, z-score -3.72)
Noise (residential + vehicle + worship) represents 3,845 complaints over 90 days—largest complaint category
Sudden week-to-week drop suggests either data lag, holiday effect, or reporting system issue rather than genuine environmental change
reporting_angles: Verify with 311 systems team whether this week's data is complete or still receiving late submissions
Determine if holiday or weather patterns explain the drop, or if it reflects a reporting artifact
